This Claim Petition is filed by the Petitioner against the Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act SCH 15 3 MVC No.431/2021 seeking Compensation of 20,00,000/ for the injuries sustained in a Road Traffic accident.

sentences.text:
2. The substance of averments made in the Petition is as under:
That on 20.12.2020 at about 6.30 p.m, when the Petitioner was proceeding as a pedestrian on the extreme left side of Tarikere - Lingadahalli road, near Aslam Pasha plant, Nandihalli, Hosahalli gate, Tarikere Taluk, Chikkamagaluru District, at that time, one Hero Honda Splendor Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA47E1050, ridden by its rider came in a rash and negligent manner, endangering to human life and without observing any traffic rules and regulations and dashed against the Petitioner from behind.
Due to the said impact, the Petitioner was fell down and sustained grievous injuries to all over the body.

Immediately after the accident, the Petitioner was shifted to Tarikere P.H.C.
Hospital and after first aid she was shifted to McGann Hospital, Shivamogga,
wherein she admitted as an inpatient.

She had spent more than Rs.1,75,000/
towards medical treatment, conveyance and nourishment charges.
4. Prior to the accident, the Petitioner was hale and healthy and she was aged about 50 years and was Tailor cum Helper at Krishna Garments, Bengaluru and was earning Rs.18,000/ per month.

The Respondent No.1 is the owner of the offending vehicle and the Respondent No. 2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle and therefore, both Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
Hence, this Petition.

2 5.

In pursuance of service of notice to the Respondents, Respondents appeared before the Court through SCH 15 5 MVC No.431/2021 their respective Counsels and the Respondent No.2 filed Objection Statement to the main petition.
Respondent No.1 did not choose to file Objection Statement to the main petition.
6. The Respondent No.2 has filed its detailed Objection Statement interalia contended that the Petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts.
Further, it stated that it has issued the Policy.

Further, it has denied the age, avocation and income of the Petitioner and the accident caused by the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending vehicle and also the injuries sustained by the Petitioner and the expenses incurred for the treatment.
Further it contended that the rider of the offending vehicle was not having valid and effective driving license and thereby violated the terms and conditions of the policy.
Therefore, it is not liable to pay the compensation to the Petitioner and has prayed to dismiss the Petition against it.
On the rival Pleadings my Learned Predecessor has framed the following Issues:
ISSUES 1.
Whether the Petitioner proves that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent act of riding of Hero Honda Splendor Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA47 E1050 and as a result, she sustained injuries?
2. Whether the Petitioner proves the age and earnings of the Petitioner as stated in the claim petition?
3. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?

4. What Order or Award?
8.
In order to prove the case of the Petitioner, the Petitioner got examined herself as P.W.1 and got marked 14 SCH 15 7 MVC No.431/2021 documents as per Ex.P1 to Ex.P14.
Further, she examined four witnesses as PW2 to PW.5 and got marked 18 documents as per Ex.P15 to Ex.P.32 and closed her side evidence.
On the other hand, Respondents did not choose to lead evidence.

9. Having heard the arguments by the learned Counsels for both sides and upon perusal of the depositions, documents exhibited and materials available on record, my answer to the above Issues are as under:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative.

3  Issue No.3 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.4 : As per the Final Order,
 for the following :
 REASONS 10.

Issue No.1 : It is the case of the Petitioner that, she had sustained grievous injuries in the Road Traffic Accident that occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the SCH 15 8 MVC No.431/2021 offending Hero Honda Splendor Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA 47E1050 by its rider.
11. On the other hand, the Respondents have denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending motorcycle.
12. In order to prove the case of the Petitioner, she got examined herself as P.W.1 and got marked 14 documents as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.14.
She also examined four witnesses by name Manjappa, Ravi Raja Shettigar, Dr.Nagaraj B.N and Gangadhar as P.W.2 to PW.5 and got marked 18 documents as per Ex.P 15 to Ex.P32.
P.W.1 has reiterated the Petition averments in her chiefaffidavit.
Ex.P1 to Ex.P8 are the True copies of FIR, Complaint, Spot Panchanama, Notice, Reply, IMV report, Wound certificate and Chargesheet.
Ex.P.9 is the Discharge summary.
Ex.P10 is the Advance Receipts.
Ex.P11 is the Prescriptions and Ex.P.12 is the Medical bills.

Upon going through Ex.P1 & Ex.P2 i.e., FIR and Complaint shows that on the complaint lodged by one Pushpavathi before Lingadahalli Police Station, the PSI of the concerned Police Station has registered the case against the rider of the Hero Honda Splendor Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA47E1050 for the offences punishable under sec. 279, 337 of IPC.
Ex.P3 is the Spot panchanama which shows that the concerned police had drawn mahazar at the spot in the presence of panchas.
Ex.P4 is the Notice.
Ex.P5 is the Reply.
Ex.P6 is the IMV report which shows that the accident does not occurred due to any mechanical defects of the vehicle.
Ex.P.7 is the Wound Certificate of the Petitioner which shows that the Petitioner had sustained simple and grievous injuries.

Ex.P8 is the Certified copy of the Charge sheet which shows that after thorough investigation, the PSI of Lingadahalli Police Station has submitted Chargesheet against the rider of the offending motorcycle for the offences punishable under Sec. 279, 337 and 338 of IPC.

Upon going through the Chargesheet i.e., Ex.P8 Column No.17 reads as under:

Ex.P9 is the Discharge summary which shows that the Petitioner was admitted as an inpatient from 24.12.2020 to 28.12.2020.
16.

Further, P.W.1 has examined Manjappa U.M., Medical Record Incharge,
Government Hospital, Tarikere as PW.2, Ravi Raja Shettygar, Medical Record Associate, Kasturba hospital as PW.3, Dr.Nagaraj B.N as P.W.4 and Gangadhar,
Medical Record Incharge, Mc.Gann Teaching District hospital, Shivamogga
as PW.5
and they produced the documents relating to the Petitioner.
PW.4 has reiterated about the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in a RTA.
17. In order to rebut the evidence of the Petitioner, the Respondent No.2 did not choose to lead evidence.
Hence, the Respondent No.2 failed to substantiate its Objection Statement contention.

The Charge sheet is the material document, which clearly shows that the said accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending SCH 15 12 MVC No.431/2021 motorcycle and nothing could be elicited to disbelieve the version of the Petitioner.

Hence, this Tribunal is of the opinion that Petitioner has proved the rash and negligent riding of the offending Hero Honda Splendor bearing Reg.No.KA47E1050 by its rider and due to the said accident, she had sustained grievous injuries.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 is in the "Affirmative".
18. Issue No. 2 & 3:
As the Petitioner has proved that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the offending motorcycle by its rider, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation.
19. In the Petition, the Petitioner has shown her age as 50 years.

Further, in the Aadhar card i.e.,
Ex.P13, date of birth of the Petitioner was shown as 01.01.1967.
The accident has taken place on 20.12.2020.
Hence, the age of the SCH 15 13 MVC No.431/2021 Petitioner, as on the date of accident was 53 years and the same is to be taken for consideration.
20 . Further, the Petitioner has averred that, she was working as Tailor cum Helper at Krishna Garments, Bengaluru and was earning Rs.18,000/ per month.
But she has not produced any document in this regard.

Therefore, in the absence of any documentary evidence, the notional Meenakashamma vs ) Chandrashekar T.S. Major on 17 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10873425/

sentences.text: Since, the accident has occurred in the year 2020, the income of the petitioner is notionally taken at Rs.14,500/ per month for the purpose of assessment of compensation.
21. With this background, the quantum of compensation to which the Petitioner is entitled may be adjudicated.

For the sake of convenience, discussion may be had under following heads:
SCH 15 14 MVC No.431/2021 I. COMPENSATION TOWARDS PAIN, SHOCK AND SUFFERING :
22.
It is stated in the petition that, in the accident, the Petitioner had sustained grievous injuries.

The Wound Certificate i.e., Ex.P7 issued by the Medical Officer of the Taluk General hospital,
Tarikere, shows that in the said accident the Petitioner had sustained two simple injuries and two grievous injuries.
The Petitioner has also examined the Dr. Nagaraj B.N. as PW.4 and he has also reiterated the injuries sustained by the Petitioner.
He has deposed that, in the said accident the Petitioner had sustained Right tibia and fibula closed fracture mid shaft and fracture of the left clavicle mid shaft.
Further he deposed about the treatment taken by the Petitioner.

23. Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that,
awarding SCH 15 15 MVC No.431/2021 compensation of Rs.75,000/ under this head would be just and reasonable.
II.
COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF AMENITIES :
24. Bearing in mind the nature of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of Rs.50,000/ under this head would be just and reasonable.
III. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF INCOME DURING THE LAID-UP PERIOD:

25. The Petitioner deposed in her evidence that she has taken the treatment at Government hospital,
Tarikere.
Upon going through Ex.P.9  Discharge summary of Kasturba hospital, Manipal, which shows that the Petitioner was admitted as an inpatient in the said hospital from 24.12.2020 to 28.12.2020.
Therefore, while calculating the total period of which the Petitioner admitted as an inpatient, it comes to 5 days.
Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that the laid up period may be considered as two months.
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.29,000/ under this head (@ Rs.14,500/ per month ).

IV. COMPENSATION TOWARDS ATTENDANT'S CHARGES, EXTRA DIET & NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE :
Meenakashamma vs ) Chandrashekar T.S. Major on 17 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10873425/
6 27.

Admittedly, the Petitioner has sustained injuries and during the laid up period, the Petitioner might have engaged an attendant and also she might have spent some amount towards extra diet and nourishment and for her conveyance.

In the facts and circumstances of the case, awarding compensation of Rs.6,000/ (@ Rs.100/ per day) towards attendants charges, Rs.6,000/
towards extra diet and nourishment and Rs.6,000/ towards conveyance would be just and reasonable.
In all, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.18,000/ under this head.
SCH 15 17 MVC No.431/2021 V.COMPENSATION TOWARDS MEDICAL EXPENCES :
28 . The Petitioner has deposed that she has spent Rs.1,75,000/ towards medical expenses and other incidental charges.
In order to prove this fact, she has produced total 19 Medical bills and hospital bills, which is marked at Ex.P.12 amounting to Rs.79,647/.
I have gone through the same and the same is acceptable.
Hence, by rounding off the same, the same to be taken at Rs.79,700/.
Hence, I am of the opinion that the Petitioner is entitled for Rs.79,700/ under this head.

COMPENSATION TOWARDS FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES:
29.
It is stated in the petition as well as in the evidence of PW.1 that she needs another surgery for the removal of implant.
PW.4 has reiterated the same in his evidence and deposed that the estimation for another surgery is around Rs.60,000/.
But he has not produced estimation.
However, by considering the further surgery for removal of implant, it is SCH 15 18 MVC No.431/2021 proper to grant compensation of 10,000/.
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.10,000/ under this head.

VI. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF FUTURE EARNINGS / COMPENSATION TOWARDS PERMANENT DISABILITY:
30.
The petitioner has stated that due to the injuries sustained by her in the accident, she has suffered permanent disablement and she is not able to do her work as she used to do earlier.
Even in her evidence, P.W.1 has deposed to that effect.

31. Further, the Petitioner got examined witness by name Dr.Nagaraj B.N as P.W.4 who has deposed regarding the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in a Road Traffic Accident and the treatment taken by the Petitioner.
Further, he has deposed that the Petitioner had disability to the whole body at 18%.
Further, PW.4 got marked Clinical notes and Xray at SCH 15 19 MVC No.431/2021 Ex.P25 and 26.
In the crossexamination, PW.4 admitted that he has not treated the Petitioner.
Further, he admitted that the fracture of the Petitioner is united and he denied the other suggestions.

Hence, by considering the nature of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that considering the disability of the Petitioner with respect to the whole body at 10% would be just and proper.
32. As per Sarla Verma's Case (2009 ACJ 1298 SC), the multiplier applicable to the Petitioner is 11.

With multiplier of 11, income of Rs.14,500/ per month and disability of the Petitioner with respect to her whole body at 10%, the loss of future income comes to  1,91,400/ (Rs.14,500/ x 12 =
Meenakashamma vs ) Chandrashekar T.S. Major on 17 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10873425/
7 1,74,000/, Rs.1,74,000/x 11 x 10/100 = 1,91,400/).
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of 1,91,400/ under this head.

SCH 15 20 MVC No.431/2021 TOTAL COMPENSATION TO WHICH THE PETITIONER IS ENTITLED:
33.

To sum up, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads :
1. Pain, shock & Suffering Rs. 75,000/
2. Loss of amenities Rs. 50,000/
3. Loss of income during the Rs. 29,000/ laid up period 4.
Attendant's charges, Extra Rs. 18,000/ diet, and conveyance 5.

Medical expenses Rs. 79,700/
6.

Future Medical Expenses Rs. 10,000/
7. Loss of Future Income Rs. 1,91,400/ Total Rs.4,53,100/
34.
Thus, totally the Petitioner is awarded compensation of Rs.4,53,100/ with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of this petition till the date of realization.
Regarding Liability:

This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent riding on the part of the rider of the Offending Hero Honda Splendor Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA47E 1050.
In this case, the Respondent No.1 is the owner and Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Further, the Respondent No.2 admitted the validity of the Insurance Policy of the offending motorcycle.
Therefore, the Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to satisfy the award amount.
The Respondent No.2, who is liable to indemnify the Respondent No.1, has to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.

Accordingly,
I answer Issue No.2 "in the Affirmative" and Issue No.3 "Partly in the Affirmative".
36. Issue No.4:

In view of my findings on Issues No. 1 to 3 , I proceed to pass the following:
 SCH 15 22 MVC No.431/2021  ORDER

The Claim Petition filed by the Meenakashamma vs ) Chandrashekar T.S. Major on 17 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10873425/
8 Petitioner against the Respondents U/S 166 of M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.

The Petitioner is entitled for Compensation of Rs.4,53,100/ along with interest at the rate of 6%
per annum from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of Award amount.
The Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.
The Respondent No.2 being the Insurer, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.

Out of the compensation amount awarded to the Petitioner, 75% of the award amount with accrued interest shall be SCH 15 23 MVC No.431/2021 released to the petitioner by way of E payment and after proper identification.
The remaining 25% award amount shall be deposited as F.D. in the name of the Petitioner in any Nationalized or Schedule bank for a period of three years.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw Award accordingly.
